A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the HQC KEM is not CCA2-secure in its current form.
the security of the HQC KEM can be reduced to the security of a code-based KEM with a small public key size, a small private key size and a small ciphertext size.
we show that HQC is vulnerable to a side-channel attack, which can be mounted on a small device with a moderate amount of side-channel traces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HQC KEM can be broken with a power analysis, and thus, it cannot achieve the CCA2 security that it is designed for.
the security analysis of the HQC proposal needs to be extended to include side-channel attacks.
the HQC KEM is vulnerable against power side-channel attacks and that its implementation should include a countermeasure.
